questions.question: Lalit deposits ₹42,000 in his account that pays an annual interest rate of 20% compounded half yearly. Calculate the total amount in his account after one year.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate is halved (10%) and the time is doubled (2 periods).

Effective rate for 2 successive cycles of 10% = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%.

**Total Amount** = 121% of 42,000.

⇒ 42,000 × 1.21 = 50,820.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50,820.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67e658ea3048af970d2b1de1d8dcd71be9529c1ebbea4018038253e6b61475ef.png] 

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹42,000**

Annual Rate (R) = **20%**

Time (T) = **1 year**

Since the interest is **compounded half yearly**:

⇒ Adjusted Rate (r) = R ÷ 2 = 20% ÷ 2 = 10% per half year

⇒ Number of periods (n) = T × 2 = 1 × 2 = 2

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 42,000 × (1 + 10/100)²

⇒ A = 42,000 × (110/100) × (110/100)

⇒ A = 42,000 × 1.1 × 1.1

⇒ A = 42,000 × 1.21

⇒ A = 50,820

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50,820.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Half-Yearly Rule

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the **annual rate** is divided by 2 and the **time (in years)** is multiplied by 2 to get the effective number of conversion periods.

Quarterly Compounding

For quarterly compounding, the rate is divided by 4 and the time is multiplied by 4. The formula becomes A = P(1 + R/400)⁴T.

Successive Percentage Change

Compound interest is an application of successive percentage change. For two periods with rate r, the effective rate is (r + r + r²/100)%.

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 14 min, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 63 min. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in min) will it take to fill one-third of the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net rate of filling = (1/14 − 1/63) = (9 − 2) / 126 = 7 / 126 = 1/18 tank/min.

Time to fill the **full tank** = 18 min.

Time to fill **1/3rd** of the tank = 18 × 1/3 = 6 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **Pipe A** (Filling) = 14 min

Time taken by **Pipe B** (Emptying) = 63 min

Let the **Total Capacity** of the tank be the **LCM** of 14 and 63.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Work (units)**
 **Efficiency (units/min)**
 
 

 Pipe A (Fill)
 14
 126
 126 ÷ 14 = 9
 
 

 Pipe B (Empty)
 63
 126 ÷ 63 = −2
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes = 9 − 2 = 7 units/min

⇒ Work to be completed = 1/3 × **Total Capacity**

⇒ Work = 1/3 × 126 = 42 units

⇒ Time taken = **Work** ÷ **Efficiency**

⇒ Time taken = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 min

**∴ The correct answer is 6 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Filling pipes have **positive efficiency**, while emptying pipes (leakage) have **negative efficiency**. Net work is the algebraic sum of efficiencies.

Time-Work Relation

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. If work is constant, Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken.

Fractional Work

To find the time for a fraction of work, multiply the **Total Time** taken for full work by that **fraction**.

questions.question: A number when increased by 110%, gives 3570. The number is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Consider the **original number** as 100%.

An **increase of 110%** makes the final percentage = 100% + 110% = 210%.

Given: 210% → 3570

Dividing by 210, we get 1% → 3570 ÷ 210 = 17.

**Original number** (100%) → 17 × 100 = 1700.

**∴ The correct answer is 1700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase = 110%

Resulting value = 3570

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Original Value × (1 + Percentage Increase / 100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d9e77d33aba9f732d6e75440ea27be1784527879501cfbb22bb33c3db211020.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original number be **x**.

⇒ x + (110 / 100) × x = 3570

⇒ x + 1.1x = 3570

⇒ 2.1x = 3570

⇒ x = 3570 / 2.1

⇒ x = 35700 / 21

⇒ x = 1700

**∴ The correct answer is 1700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase Formula

New Value = Original Value × (100 + Increase%) ÷ 100. This is the standard method for **growth calculations**.

Reverse Percentage

To find the original value when the increased value is known, divide the final value by the **multiplying factor** (e.g., 2.1 for 110% increase).

Fractional Equivalence

An increase of 110% is equivalent to multiplying the number by 21/10 or 2.1. This helps in **fast mental math**.

questions.question: If the fourth proportional to 2x, 3x, and 12 is y, find y.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of the first two terms **2x : 3x** simplifies to **2 : 3**.

For **proportion**, the ratio of the next two terms **12 : y** must also be **2 : 3**.

Comparing the parts: **2 units = 12** ⇒ **1 unit = 6**.

Therefore, **y = 3 units = 3 × 6 = 18**.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The terms are **2x**, **3x**, **12**, and **y** is the **fourth proportional**.

**Formula Used:** If **a, b, c, d** are in **proportion**, then **a/b = c/d**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff08aba64d3ca096d0117f7dda9cd626789875492ccb9072e31e4938e534dbeb.png] 

⇒ 2x ÷ 3x = 12 ÷ y

⇒ 2 ÷ 3 = 12 ÷ y

⇒ 2 × y = 12 × 3

⇒ 2y = 36

⇒ y = 36 ÷ 2

⇒ y = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is calculated as **√(a × b)**.

Third Proportional

If **a, b, c** are in continued proportion, then **a/b = b/c**, where **c = b² ÷ a** is the third proportional.

Product Rule

In any proportion **a : b :: c : d**, the **product of extremes (a × d)** is always equal to the **product of means (b × c)**.

questions.question:
What is the mode of the following data?

43, 44, 43, 53, 42, 44, 46, 47, 55, 50, 52, 55, 40, 45, 44, 53, 48, 48
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Mode** of a data set is the value that appears most **frequently**.

By scanning the given numbers: **44** appears 3 times (at positions 2, 6, and 15).

Other frequent values like 43, 53, 55, and 48 appear only 2 times each.

Since 44 has the highest count, it is the mode.

**∴ The correct answer is 44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data set = {43, 44, 43, 53, 42, 44, 46, 47, 55, 50, 52, 55, 40, 45, 44, 53, 48, 48}

**Formula Used:** Mode = The observation with the **Maximum Frequency**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5e8c24f88b279dc0ee1773bdd4b7c129477b4aebb18baed5e8b601e4de7da36.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Count of 40 = 1

⇒ Count of 42 = 1

⇒ Count of 43 = 2

⇒ Count of 44 = 3

⇒ Count of 45 = 1

⇒ Count of 46 = 1

⇒ Count of 47 = 1

⇒ Count of 48 = 2

⇒ Count of 50 = 1

⇒ Count of 52 = 1

⇒ Count of 53 = 2

⇒ Count of 55 = 2

⇒ The maximum frequency is 3, which corresponds to the value **44**.

**∴ The correct answer is 44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean (Arithmetic Average)

It is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations: Mean = (∑xᵢ) ÷ n.

Median

The **middle value** of the data when arranged in ascending or descending order. For n = 18 (even), it is the average of the 9th and 10th terms.

Empirical Relationship

In a moderately asymmetrical distribution, the relationship is: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Range

The difference between the **maximum** and **minimum** values in the data set: Range = Max − Min.

questions.question: A trader claims to sell spice at a profit of 15% but also dishonestly uses a weight which is 14% less than what is mentioned on it. Find the total percentage of profit earned by the trader. (Round the answer to the nearest whole number)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Profit Percentage** = [ (100 + **Profit%**) / (100 − **Less Weight%**) − 1 ] × 100

Total Profit % = [ (100 + 15) / (100 − 14) − 1 ] × 100

Total Profit % = [ 115 / 86 − 1 ] × 100 = (29 / 86) × 100

Total Profit % ≈ 33.72%

Rounding to the **nearest whole number**, we get 34%.

**∴ The correct answer is 34%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Claimed **Profit** = 15%

Dishonest **Weight reduction** = 14%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4fe9a0f90f74f16a10d497c480ca6944be1276096b975e31c7d3439c849056e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1000g spice be ₹1000.

⇒ Trader sells at 15% profit, so **Selling Price (SP)** = 1000 + 15% of 1000 = ₹1150.

⇒ Trader uses 14% less weight, so **Actual weight** given = 1000 − 14% of 1000 = 860g.

⇒ **Cost Price** for the trader for 860g = ₹860.

⇒ Total **Profit** = SP − Actual CP = 1150 − 860 = ₹290.

⇒ Total **Profit %** = (Profit / Actual CP) × 100

⇒ Total Profit % = (290 / 860) × 100 = 2900 / 86 ≈ 33.7209%.

⇒ Rounding to the nearest whole number → 34%.

**∴ The correct answer is 34%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

Profit % = [ (True Weight − Faulty Weight) / Faulty Weight ] × 100. When both profit margin and faulty weight are involved, use the ratio of multipliers.

Successive Percentage for Profit

Total Gain % = [ (1 + g₁/100)(1 + g₂/100) − 1 ] × 100, where g₁ is the price gain and g₂ is the gain from weight manipulation.

Effective Weight Gain

If a trader cheats by x% while buying and y% while selling using faulty weights, the net profit is calculated based on the actual quantity handled relative to the stated price.

questions.question: Mr.John spent 20% of his monthly income on food and 20% on children's education. 40% of the remaining income, he spent on shopping and transport together and 20% of the rest was spent on medical expenses. If he is left with ₹23,040, after all these expenditures, what is his monthly income?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Total spend on **Food** and **Education** = 20% + 20% = 40% → Remaining = 60% (3/5) Remaining after **Shopping/Transport** = 60% × (100% − 40%) = 36% (9/25) Remaining after **Medical** = 36% × (100% − 20%) = 28.8% (36/125) 28.8% of Income = ₹23,040 Total Income = 23,040 ÷ 0.288 = 80,000 **∴ The correct answer is ₹80,000.**

questions.question: If the product of two numbers is 98,304 and their HCF is 128, then find the LCM of the numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Formula: **LCM = Product ÷ HCF**

Substitute the values: **LCM = 98,304 ÷ 128**

Shortcut (Unit Digit Method): The unit digit of the product is 4 and the HCF is 8. Since 8 × 8 = 64, the unit digit of the **LCM** must be 8.

Checking options: Only 768 ends with 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 768.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Product of **two numbers** = 98,304

**HCF** (Highest Common Factor) = 128

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = **HCF × LCM**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d020489486c8e0464f151ca3fe04bc1a2e548ea59b8b94b508a6b053d2cf939.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 98,304 = 128 × **LCM**

⇒ LCM = 98,304 ÷ 128

⇒ LCM = 768

**∴ The correct answer is 768.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Relation

For any **two numbers** x and y, their Product = HCF(x, y) × LCM(x, y). This specific identity does not hold true for three or more numbers.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

LCM of Fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators). HCF of Fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators).

Divisibility Rule

The **LCM** of any set of numbers is always exactly divisible by the **HCF** of that same set of numbers.

questions.question: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 60 years. Five years ago from now, the product of numerical values of their ages was 525. Find the present age (in years) of the father.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Options Elimination** method for the **Father's age**.

If **Father's present age** is 40 years, then **Son's present age** = 60 − 40 = 20 years.

5 years ago: **Father** = 40 − 5 = 35 years and **Son** = 20 − 5 = 15 years.

Check the **Product of numerical values**: 35 × 15 = 525.

This matches the given condition exactly.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

questions.question: When one-third of a number is increased by 25, the result is 100. Find the sum of the digits of the original number.
questions.solution:
Logic followed here is.

Logic: Convert the mathematical statement into a **linear equation** to find the **original number**, and then calculate the **sum of its digits**.

**Step 1: Finding the original number**

Let the **original number** be **x**.

According to the given condition, **one-third** of the number increased by **25** results in **100**.

The equation is: **(x / 3) + 25 = 100**

Subtracting **25** from both sides:

**x / 3 = 100 − 25**

**x / 3 = 75**

Multiplying by **3** to find **x**:

**x = 75 × 3**

**x = 225**

 

**Step 2: Calculating the sum of the digits**

The **original number** obtained is **225**.

 
 

 **Digit 1**
 **Digit 2**
 **Digit 3**
 
 

 2
 2
 5
 
 

Sum of the digits = **2 + 2 + 5 = 9**

 

Therefore, the sum of the digits of the original number is **9**.

questions.question: If 9A7B is divisible by 55, find A + B.
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ A number is **divisible by 55** if it is divisible by both **5 and 11**. Applying the **divisibility rule of 11**: Sum of alternate digits difference must be 0 or 11. ⇒ (9 + 7) − (A + B) = 16 − (A + B) For the number to be divisible by 11, 16 − (A + B) = 11 (since 16 − (A + B) = 0 gives A + B = 16, which doesn't satisfy single-digit constraints for both cases of B). ⇒ A + B = 16 − 11 = 5 **∴ The correct answer is 5.**

questions.question: The difference between the present ages of Ayushi and Nidhi is 21 years. Five years ago from now, the sum of their ages was 83 years. If Ayushi is older than Nidhi, find Nidhi's present age (in years).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present **Sum** of ages = **Sum** 5 years ago + (2 × 5) = 83 + 10 = 93 years.

The **Difference** between ages always remains constant, so **Difference** = 21 years.

Since **Ayushi** is older, **Nidhi's** age (younger) = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2.

**Nidhi's** present age = (93 − 21) ÷ 2 = 72 ÷ 2 = 36 years.

questions.question: A 180-meter-long train passes a pole in 12 seconds. A second 120-meter-long train is moving in the same direction as of the first train and crosses the first train in 15 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed** of first train = 180 / 12 = 15 m/s.

**Relative Speed** = (Total Length) ÷ Time = (180 + 120) / 15 = 300 / 15 = 20 m/s.

In **same direction**, Relative Speed = Speed₂ − Speed₁.

Speed of second train = 20 + 15 = 35 m/s.

Convert to **km/h**: 35 × (18/5) = 126 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 126 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 180 m

Time to pass a **stationary pole** = 12 sec

Length of second train (L₂) = 120 m

Time to cross each other in **same direction** = 15 sec

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/11f4958787cac0b5134031a0a7a3401aee8bf2cd8012223fa8176ef381c35d61.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of first train (v₁) = Length / Time

⇒ v₁ = 180 / 12 = 15 m/s

⇒ Total distance covered during crossing = L₁ + L₂

⇒ Total Distance = 180 + 120 = 300 m

⇒ Relative Speed (v₂ − v₁) = Total Distance / Time of crossing

⇒ v₂ − 15 = 300 / 15

⇒ v₂ − 15 = 20

⇒ v₂ = 20 + 15 = 35 m/s

⇒ Speed of second train in **km/h** = 35 × (18/5)

⇒ Speed = 7 × 18 = 126 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 126 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the **difference** of their speeds (V₁ − V₂). If they move in **opposite directions**, it is the **sum** (V₁ + V₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5. To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18.

Crossing Distance

When a train crosses another train, the **total distance** covered is always the **sum of the lengths** of both trains, regardless of the direction of motion.

questions.question: Simplify: ((120 - 12) div (24 div 2) - 12 + 7)/(5 times 12 div 10 - (6 times 4) div 12)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the **Numerator** and **Denominator** independently using the **BODMAS rule**.

**Numerator**: (108 ÷ 12) − 12 + 7 ⇒ 9 − 12 + 7 = 4

**Denominator**: (60 ÷ 10) − (24 ÷ 12) ⇒ 6 − 2 = 4

Simplified result = 4 ÷ 4 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: ((120 − 12) ÷ (24 ÷ 2) − 12 + 7) / (5 × 12 ÷ 10 − (6 × 4) ÷ 12)

**Formula Used:**

The **BODMAS rule** defines the order of operations: **Brackets**, **Of**, **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Numerator = (120 − 12) ÷ (24 ÷ 2) − 12 + 7

⇒ Numerator = 108 ÷ 12 − 12 + 7

⇒ Numerator = 9 − 12 + 7 = 4

⇒ Denominator = (5 × 12 ÷ 10) − (6 × 4 ÷ 12)

⇒ Denominator = (60 ÷ 10) − (24 ÷ 12)

⇒ Denominator = 6 − 2 = 4

⇒ Final Expression = 4 / 4 = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Always solve **Brackets** first (round (), then curly {}, then square []), followed by **Division** and **Multiplication** (from left to right), and finally **Addition** and **Subtraction**.

Fraction Simplification

When simplifying complex fractions, treat the **Numerator** and **Denominator** as separate expressions and simplify them completely before performing the final division.

Operator Precedence

Multiplication and division hold the same level of precedence; if both appear, solve the expression starting from the **left side** to the **right side**.

questions.question: If the area of an equilateral triangle is given as 900 m², then what is its perimeter?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Area** of an equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × **side**² ⇒ 900 = (√3/4) × a².

**side** (a) = √(3600 / √3) = 60 / 3¹/⁴.

**Perimeter** = 3 × **side** = 3 × (60 / 3¹/⁴) = 60 × 3¹ − ¹/⁴ = 60 × 3³/⁴.

Since 3³/⁴ = (3³)¹/⁴ = 27¹/⁴ = ⁴√27.

**∴ The correct answer is 60⁴√27 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Area** of the equilateral triangle = 900 m².

**Formula Used:** **Area** = (√3 / 4) × a² | **Perimeter** = 3a (where a = **side**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca8c619c822d1dd239445bdcd2994655fcc1ff58d3202b7315a7a395fd4dbfad.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 900 = (√3 / 4) × a²

⇒ a² = (900 × 4) / √3

⇒ a² = 3600 / 3¹/²

⇒ a = √(3600 / 3¹/²) = 60 / (3¹/²)¹/²

⇒ a = 60 / 3¹/⁴

⇒ **Perimeter** = 3 × a = 3 × (60 / 3¹/⁴)

⇒ **Perimeter** = 60 × (3¹ / 3¹/⁴) = 60 × 3⁽¹ − ¹/⁴⁾

⇒ **Perimeter** = 60 × 3³/⁴ = 60 × (3³)¹/⁴

⇒ **Perimeter** = 60⁴√27 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 60⁴√27 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Height of Equilateral Triangle

The **altitude** or **height** (h) is given by h = (√3 / 2) × a.

Inradius and Circumradius

For an equilateral triangle, **Inradius** (r) = a / (2√3) and **Circumradius** (R) = a / √3.

Area in terms of Height

The **Area** can also be calculated using its height as **Area** = h² / √3.

Properties

In an equilateral triangle, all three **internal angles** are equal to 60°, and the **centroid**, **orthocenter**, **circumcenter**, and **incenter** all coincide.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is NOT divisible by both 6 and 9?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number **divisible** by both 6 and 9 must be a multiple of their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

**LCM** of 6 and 9 ⇒ 18.

Check the given options for multiples of 18: 18, 36, **54**, **72**, **90**...

45 is not a multiple of 18 as 18 × 2.5 = 45.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

To be **divisible by both 6 and 9**, a number must be **even** (divisible by 2), its sum of digits must be divisible by 3 (for 6), and its sum of digits must be divisible by 9.

**Given Numbers:** 54, 45, 90, 72

**Step 1: Check Divisibility by 6 (Divisible by 2 and 3)**

⇒ 54: Ends in 4 (Even) and 5 + 4 = 9 (Divisible by 3) → **Divisible by 6**.

⇒ 45: Ends in 5 (Odd) → **NOT divisible by 6**.

⇒ 90: Ends in 0 (Even) and 9 + 0 = 9 (Divisible by 3) → **Divisible by 6**.

⇒ 72: Ends in 2 (Even) and 7 + 2 = 9 (Divisible by 3) → **Divisible by 6**.

**Step 2: Check Divisibility by 9 (Sum of digits divisible by 9)**

⇒ 54: 5 + 4 = 9 → **Divisible by 9**.

⇒ 45: 4 + 5 = 9 → **Divisible by 9**.

⇒ 90: 9 + 0 = 9 → **Divisible by 9**.

⇒ 72: 7 + 2 = 9 → **Divisible by 9**.

Since 45 is divisible by 9 but **NOT** by 6, it is the correct choice.

**∴ The correct answer is 45.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is simultaneously divisible by both **2** (last digit is 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8) and **3** (sum of digits is a multiple of 3).

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of its digits** is completely divisible by 9.

LCM Method for Combined Divisibility

To check divisibility by multiple numbers, find the **LCM** of those numbers; any common multiple must be divisible by this LCM.

questions.question: Simplify: [{76 times (24 div 3) + 2 times 18} div 644] times (20)/(2)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the given expression using the **BODMAS rule** by simplifying inner parts first.

Simplify **Parentheses** and **Division**: (24 ÷ 3) = 8 and (20 ÷ 2) = 10.

Solve **Curly Braces**: {76 × 8 + 2 × 18} = {608 + 36} = 644.

Complete the **Square Brackets** and final **Multiplication**: [644 ÷ 644] × 10 = 1 × 10 = 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** [{76 × (24 ÷ 3) + 2 × 18} ÷ 644] × (20)/(2)

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS Rule** (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ [{76 × 8 + 2 × 18} ÷ 644] × 10

⇒ [{608 + 36} ÷ 644] × 10

⇒ [644 ÷ 644] × 10

⇒ 1 × 10

⇒ 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

The **BODMAS rule** dictates the order of operations: **Brackets**, **Of** (powers/roots), **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Bracket Hierarchy

Always solve expressions in the order of **Circular Brackets** ( ), then **Curly Braces** { }, and finally **Square Brackets** [ ].

Division and Multiplication

While **Division** and **Multiplication** are often grouped, they must be performed strictly as per the priority order or left-to-right to avoid calculation errors.

questions.question: Three pipes X, Y, and Z can fill a tank in 12, 15, and 20 hours, respectively. All three pipes are opened together but pipe Z is closed 3 hours before the tank is completely filled. In how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(12, 15, 20) = **60 units**. Efficiencies: X = **5**, Y = **4**, Z = **3**.

If a pipe is closed **3 hr before** completion, add its potential work to the total work.

New Total Work = 60 + (3 × 3) = **69 units**.

Total time = 69 ÷ (5 + 4 + 3) = 69 ÷ 12 = **5.75 hr**.

5.75 hr = 5 hr + (0.75 × 60) min = **5 hr 45 min**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 hr 45 min.**

questions.question: What sum of money (in ₹) will yield ₹720 as simple interest in 3 years at 8% per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage = **Rate** × **Time** = 8% × 3 = 24%.

Given that 24% of the **Principal** is equal to ₹720.

⇒ 1% of **Principal** = 720 ÷ 24 = 30.

⇒ 100% (**Sum of money**) = 30 × 100 = ₹3000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Simple Interest (SI)** = ₹720

**Time (T)** = 3 years

**Rate (R)** = 8% p.a.

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest (SI)** = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48bf563a4c2b42f79f74c2a41aa7663af7fb21eaba1bd166848acea7f03aa8cd.png] 

⇒ 720 = (P × 8 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 720 = (P × 24) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (720 × 100) ÷ 24

⇒ P = 30 × 100

⇒ P = ₹3000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount

The total sum of money payable at the end of the time period is A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Simple Interest Characteristics

Unlike compound interest, simple interest is always calculated only on the initial **Principal** amount, meaning the interest remains constant for every year if the rate is fixed.

Rate of Interest Formula

To find the annual rate when other variables are known: R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T).

questions.question: If a + b + c = 13 and ab + bc + ca = 4, then what is the value of ab(a + b) + bc(b + c) + ca(c + a) + 3abc?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **c = 0** as there are 3 variables and only 2 equations.

From the given: **a + b = 13** and **ab = 4**.

The expression reduces to **ab(a + b) + 0 + 0 + 0**.

Substituting the values: **4 × 13 = 52**.

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **a + b + c = 13** and **ab + bc + ca = 4**.

From **a + b + c = 13**, we can derive:

⇒ **a + b = 13 − c**

⇒ **b + c = 13 − a**

⇒ **c + a = 13 − b**

Now, substitute these into the required expression **ab(a + b) + bc(b + c) + ca(c + a) + 3abc**:

⇒ ab(**13 − c**) + bc(**13 − a**) + ca(**13 − b**) + 3abc

⇒ 13ab − abc + 13bc − abc + 13ca − abc + 3abc

⇒ 13(ab + bc + ca) − 3abc + 3abc

⇒ 13(**4**)

⇒ **52**

**∴ The correct answer is 52.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square of a Trinomial

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca). This identity relates the sum of terms, sum of squares, and sum of products taken two at a time.

Sum of Cubes Identity

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca). If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Value Assumption Method

In competitive exams, if an expression is symmetric and there are more variables than equations, setting one variable to **0** or **1** often leads to a quick solution.

questions.question: The mean of a data is 47 and its median is 61. The mode (using empirical relation) of the data is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Empirical Relation** for moderately skewed distributions: **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Substitute the given values: Mode = 3 × 61 − 2 × 47.

Mode = 183 − 94 = 89.

**∴ The correct answer is 89.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mean** of the data = 47

**Median** of the data = 61

**Formula Used:**

The **Empirical Relationship** between the three measures of central tendency is:

**Mode = 3(Median) − 2(Mean)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4c28f845a09cc8cbca31ba4726cfb76b0c90e6e1dae06bf3dd44b833d7b4bd8e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mode = 3 × 61 − 2 × 47

⇒ Mode = 183 − 94

⇒ Mode = 89

**∴ The correct answer is 89.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution** (like the Normal Distribution), the values of **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all identical (Mean = Median = Mode).

Positively Skewed Distribution

In a **positively skewed** (right-skewed) distribution, the values generally follow the order: **Mean > Median > Mode**.

Negatively Skewed Distribution

In a **negatively skewed** (left-skewed) distribution, the values generally follow the order: **Mean < Median < Mode**.

Karl Pearson Formula

The empirical relation can also be expressed as: **(Mean − Mode) = 3 × (Mean − Median)**, which is useful for calculating the coefficient of skewness.

questions.question: A dealer buys two articles X and Y for ₹800 each. He marks each of them at the same price. He sells X by giving two successive discounts of 73% and 37% and still earns ₹901 as profit. If he sells Y at a single discount of 89%, then what is the profit percentage on Y?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **Selling Price (SP)** of article X = 800 + 901 = ₹1701. Effective multiplier for successive discounts of 73% and 37% = 0.27 × 0.63 = 0.1701. **Marked Price (MP)** = 1701 ÷ 0.1701 = ₹10000. **SP** of article Y = 10000 × (100% − 89%) = 10000 × 0.11 = ₹1100. **Profit %** on Y = ((1100 − 800) ÷ 800) × 100 = 3/8 × 100 = 37.5%. **∴ The correct answer is 37.50%.**

questions.question: The difference between two parallel sides of a trapezium is 9 cm. The perpendicular distance between them is 52 cm. If the area of the trapezium is 988 cm ², find the lengths of the parallel sides (in cm).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **parallel sides** = (2 × **Area**) ÷ **Height**

Sum = (2 × 988) ÷ 52 = 1976 ÷ 52 = 38 cm

Larger side = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (38 + 9) ÷ 2 = 23.5 cm

Smaller side = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (38 − 9) ÷ 2 = 14.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 23.5, 14.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of **trapezium** = 988 cm²

**Perpendicular distance** (h) = 52 cm

Difference between **parallel sides** (a − b) = 9 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd1f805133eadbc2c087e91ca476e385aef85c21176475d5b41e82f0b899e7f1.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × (Distance between them)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the parallel sides be **a** and **b**.

⇒ a − b = 9 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (a + b) × 52 = 988

⇒ (a + b) × 26 = 988

⇒ a + b = 988 ÷ 26

⇒ a + b = 38 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding Eq. 1 and Eq. 2: 2a = 47

⇒ a = 47 ÷ 2 = 23.5 cm

⇒ Subtracting Eq. 1 from Eq. 2: 2b = 29

⇒ b = 29 ÷ 2 = 14.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 23.5, 14.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Trapezium

The area is calculated as Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × height.

Median of a Trapezium

The segment connecting the midpoints of the non-parallel sides. Length = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Isosceles Trapezium

A trapezium where the non-parallel sides are equal and the base angles are equal.

Perimeter of Trapezium

The sum of all four sides: P = a + b + c + d.

questions.question: The length of a diagonal of a rectangular park is 25 meters, and that of one of its sides is 15 meters. Find the perimeter of the park.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **Pythagorean triplet** ratio 3 : 4 : 5.

Given **Side** = 15 (3 × 5) and **Diagonal** = 25 (5 × 5).

Other **Side** = 4 × 5 = 20 m.

**Perimeter** = 2 × (Length + Breadth) = 2 × (15 + 20) = 70 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Diagonal** (d) of **rectangular park** = 25 m

One **side** (l) = 15 m

**Formula Used:**

**Pythagorean Theorem**: d² = l² + b²

**Perimeter** = 2 × (l + b)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e8c24648d8376cfaed5231082b527519d72a7f4a9658b1faa232feac4812a251.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 25² = 15² + b²

⇒ 625 = 225 + b²

⇒ b² = 625 − 225

⇒ b² = 400

⇒ b = √400 = 20 m

⇒ **Perimeter** = 2 × (15 + 20)

⇒ **Perimeter** = 2 × 35 = 70 m

**∴ The correct answer is 70 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The **area** is the product of its **length** and **breadth**: Area = l × b.

Properties of Rectangles

All internal angles are 90° and **diagonals** are equal in length and bisect each other.

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Frequently used triplets in exams include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Diagonal of a Square

For a square of side 'a', the **diagonal** is always a√2.
